lines.text: Three years to cut one diamond.
In 1986, South Africa's Premier Mine gave up a 599 carat crystal.
lines.say: In nineteen eighty six, South Africa's Premier Mine gave up a five hundred ninety nine carat crystal.

lines.text: De Beers showed it at its 100th anniversary celebration in 1988.
lines.say: De Beers showed it at its one hundredth anniversary celebration in nineteen eighty eight.

lines.text: It was named the Centenary Diamond for that anniversary.
Master cutter Gabi Tolkowsky led the cutting team.
The first 154 days went to cutting away flawed material by hand.
lines.say: The first one hundred fifty four days went to cutting away flawed material by hand.

lines.text: Cutting and polishing took about three years in all.
The finished diamond weighs 273.85 carats and has 247 facets.
lines.say: The finished diamond weighs two hundred seventy three point eight five carats and has two hundred forty seven facets.

lines.text: Its heart shape has no cleft at the top.
It was first shown in London in May 1991.
lines.say: It was first shown in London in May nineteen ninety one.

post.caption: The Centenary Diamond took about three years to cut. In 1986, South Africa's Premier Mine gave up a 599 carat crystal, and De Beers showed it at its 100th anniversary celebration in 1988. Master cutter Gabi Tolkowsky led the team, and the first 154 days went to cutting away flawed material by hand. The finished diamond weighs 273.85 carats and has 247 facets, in a heart shape without the cleft at the top. It was first shown in London in May 1991.
